purpose: Identify how extracted Ontario Annual Practice authorities connect, where duplication risks exist, and what must be preserved before coding.
nonNegotiableFindings: All rules must flow through MasterCaseSchema.
No engine may become a second source of truth.
No rule may be coded as a shallow checklist if it affects strategy, evidence, risk, costs, or readiness.
Every recommendation must be traceable to authority, facts, risk, and confidence.

mustNotDuplicate: separate issue map outside pleading record
motion checklist separate from evidence proof map
offer tracker separate from costs exposure
costs engine separate from conduct engine

highestDuplicationRisks.why: Service, defence, motion, affidavit, pre-trial, assessment, and offer deadlines all create timers.
highestDuplicationRisks.solution: One DeadlineEngine; rule-specific deadlines are DeadlineObjects only.

highestDuplicationRisks.why: Rule30 documents, Rule31 discovery answers, Rule39 affidavit evidence, and Rule50 trial documents overlap.
Rule49, Rule57, and Rule58 all affect costs.
highestDuplicationRisks.solution: One LitigationRiskCostsSettlementEngine with submodules, not three independent engines.

highestDuplicationRisks.why: Summary judgment readiness, motion readiness, discovery readiness, and trial readiness are related.
highestDuplicationRisks.solution: One Readiness framework with stage-specific readiness assessments.

codingReadinessConclusion.reason: Need engine-by-engine implementation map and MasterCaseSchema field map first.
